headline: Cluster-stratified results are exploratory; mouse remains the experimental unit.

primaryFindings.title: Cluster-matched neoplastic nuclear eccentricity
primaryFindings.question: Does the Vehicle-versus-PLX contrast persist within commonly supported tile phenotypes?
primaryFindings.summary: Fully supported fine-stratum deltas: C0 +0.009619 (two-sided p=0.333, LOMO same-sign); C1 +0.006466 (two-sided p=0.667, LOMO mixed); C2 -0.001786 (two-sided p=1.000, LOMO mixed); C4 +0.002607 (two-sided p=0.889, LOMO mixed); C6 -0.017941 (two-sided p=0.278, LOMO same-sign). No robust shared direction is established.
primaryFindings.interpretation: The cluster-specific directions are heterogeneous, so these data do not support a cluster-invariant treatment effect; report the strata rather than a single positive story.

primaryFindings.title: Composition-standardised eccentricity
primaryFindings.question: What is the contrast after giving every mouse the same eligible-cluster mixture?
primaryFindings.summary: Composition-standardised deltas: equal -0.007667 (two-sided p=0.722, LOMO mixed); pooled_reference -0.005937 (two-sided p=0.722, LOMO mixed). Positive averages are not mouse-robust.
primaryFindings.interpretation: The standardised estimates and/or cluster-specific estimates do not share one direction, so no composition-invariant treatment story is supported.

primaryFindings.title: Frozen outcome-blind cluster resolution
primaryFindings.question: Is clustering stable and interpretable?
primaryFindings.summary: K=7 is the frozen run-local resolution. Stability, one-SE, under-segmentation review and K lineage are audited on the cluster-selection page; treatment labels and nucleus outcomes were not used to select K.
primaryFindings.interpretation: K is a practical exploratory resolution, not a uniquely proven biological taxonomy.

primaryFindings.title: Recurrence, semantic review and nuisance
primaryFindings.question: Are clusters recurring tissue phenotypes or slide/stain signatures?
primaryFindings.summary: All 3 fine clusters occur in all 8 slides, but their fractions are uneven and the neutral technical roles remain provisional. Thumbnail colour/focus diagnostics do not replace stain-normalised or independent-slide validation.
primaryFindings.interpretation: Recurring membership does not rule out stain, scanner, section or mouse identity effects.

primaryFindings.title: Tissue-cluster composition
primaryFindings.question: Does treatment associate with tissue-cluster composition?
primaryFindings.summary: No macroregion contrast has same-sign leave-one-mouse-out support (2/3). Largest same-sign fine candidate is C0 at +14.44 percentage points; it remains compositional and exploratory.
primaryFindings.interpretation: Cluster fractions sum to one and are not independent treatment effects.

primaryFindings.title: Within-tumour cluster profiles
primaryFindings.question: How do nuclei differ between clusters within each tumour?
primaryFindings.summary: Raw mouse-by-cluster profiles show marked differences in cell composition, density and nuclear morphology. Optional deviations use only endpoint-eligible non-background strata.
primaryFindings.interpretation: These contrasts help describe cluster content but are partly circular because the clusters were learned from H&E morphology; they are not treatment tests.

primaryFindings.title: Sensitivity synthesis
primaryFindings.question: Are signals robust to K, weighting, boundary exclusion and segmentation QC?
primaryFindings.summary: K±1, unweighted clustering, 10/20-pixel boundary exclusions and cell-weighted variants remain visible. They do not restore a shared eccentricity direction across fine strata; composition-standardised leave-one-mouse-out directions remain mixed.
primaryFindings.interpretation: Secondary density and solidity patterns require independent segmentation and tissue-area validation.

primaryFindings.title: Current conclusion
primaryFindings.question: What can and cannot be concluded?
primaryFindings.summary: The analysis supports heterogeneous tissue contexts and candidate cluster-specific patterns, not a statistically established, cluster-invariant or drug-induced nuclear phenotype.
primaryFindings.interpretation: Mouse is the experimental unit; two mice per arm within each cohort and one WSI per mouse preclude causal separation from slide identity or cohort-linked batch effects.

robustness.label: Boundary sensitivity
robustness.note: 10px and 20px ambiguous-boundary exclusions are separate sensitivity estimates.

robustness.label: Aggregation sensitivity
robustness.note: Tile-balanced primary and nucleus-count-weighted tile-summary sensitivity are both reported.

robustness.label: Selected-K weighting sensitivity
robustness.note: Compares inverse-mouse-weighted labels with selected-K unweighted labels when available.

limitations: Only two mice per arm within each cohort; one WSI per mouse, so mouse and slide are confounded.
Clusters are learned from the same 8 slides and may encode stain/scanner or individual-slide identity.
Cohort, cell line, processing batch and UNI-v2 inference backend are confounded; the combined view is exploratory and inference is cohort-blocked.
Tile density uses full 256px tile area and is approximate for partially tissue-covered edge tiles.
The optional tissue-fraction correction uses a compressed 48px JPEG atlas proxy, not raw-slide tissue segmentation; background/edge density must not support a strong biological conclusion.
Axis ratio is derived deterministically from eccentricity and is a sensitivity reparameterisation, not independent corroboration.
Multiple cluster/metric views are exploratory; they are not independent replications.
Thousands of metric, threshold, K, boundary and aggregation views were explored without multiplicity correction.
CellViT segmentation and cell-type calls have not been independently validated for slide/stain sensitivity in these 8 WSIs.
Inflammation+Connective is a composite class and cannot be interpreted as immune infiltration alone.
Cluster fractions are compositional parts constrained to sum to one.
Tile-balanced morphology averages per-tile quantiles; cell-weighted sensitivity averages those tile quantiles by contributing nucleus count and is not a pooled single-cell median.

unavailable.reason: blinded QC showed pure-white/background exemplars can have tissue_fraction_proxy near 0.94; the compressed 48px JPEG threshold is not a reliable tissue-area estimate
unavailable.full_tile_density_interpretation: approximate counts per full tile area only; edge/background tiles are not tissue-area densities

reviewFlags.label: Pathology review
reviewFlags.note: Do not give anatomical or drug-effect names to unreviewed clusters.

reviewFlags.label: Stain/slide sensitivity
reviewFlags.note: Thumbnail colour/focus and mouse-share diagnostics were run, but stain normalisation or independent-slide validation was not; confounding remains plausible.

recommendedLanguage: no cluster-invariant treatment effect is supported
hypothesis-generating with two mice per arm within each of two cohort blocks
prohibitedClaims: millions of nuclei as independent replicates
background/edge full-tile density as true tissue density
axis ratio as independent confirmation of eccentricity
